3. According to the plaintiff the above suit was filed out of time by 165 days and as such a separate application has been filed for condonation of delay. After hearing the application for condonation of delay in filing the aforesaid suit, an order was passed by the Admiralty Court on 6.4.88 to the effect that subject to just objection that may be taken at the time of hearing by the other side as to limitation, 'let the suit be admitted for hearing and plaint be registered. 

 4. The defendant is contesting the suit by filling written statement contending, inter alia, that there is no cause of action for filing the aforesaid suit. The suit is barred by limitation and the same is not maintainable in view of the fact that the proceeding under section 52 of Ordinance 72/76 is pending on the self-same subject matter wherein the plaintiff is entitled to seek appropriate redress regarding the alleged damage of its vessel. Further, the defendant has denied the other allegations made in the plaint. 

 2.	It the suit barred by limitation? 

 6.	The defendant filed an application on 25.1.90 praying for hearing the first 2 issues namely, whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and whether it is barred by limitation. This application was heard by this court and a formal order was passed 28.1.90 allowing the aforesaid prayer of the defendant and fixing 5.2.90 for hearing the aforesaid 2 preliminary issues. 

 11. Mr. Khondker next submits that the suit is barred by limitation and to raise the question of limitation at this stage is open to him though the plaint was accepted and the suit was registered. Mr. Khondker has drawn my attention to paragraph No. 5 of the application for extension of time under section 8 of the Maritime Convention Act. 1911. In that paragraph it is stated that when the defendant failed to pay the compensation after repeated reminders the plaintiff took decision on 22.8.87 to file a suit. He submits that this decision to file a suit is also out of time because the limitation to me such a suit is for 2 years from the date of incident. I have perused the plaint the application for condonation of delay as well as written statement filed by the parties. In the application for condonation of delay the grounds set forth explaining the delay of 165 days are not at all satisfactory and the same cannot be accepted. It is required that reasonable explanation must be given for each and every day's delay inasmuch as after the period of limitation the right of the other party accrues in the matter and as such it should not be lightly dealt with. The explanation as regards change of legal adviser of the plaintiff is not at all convincing and for such reason in my view delay of such a long period needs no consideration. In the facts and circumstances of the case I am of the view that Mr. Khondker succeeds in both the points. In the result the suit is dismissed. But the judgment of this Court shall not in any way prejudice the interest of any party in the proceeding pending before the Marine Court and the Marine Court is at liberty to proceed with the proceeding in accordance with law. There shall be no order as to costs.
